Drama and Theatre Studies
Drama A Level
Examining Board: OCR
Overview
Drama and Theatre is a dynamic and creative course that develops confidence, communication and collaboration. Students explore how theatre is created through acting, directing, design and performance, while developing valuable analytical and evaluative skills.
Through practical workshops, live theatre visits and academic study, students engage with a wide variety of theatrical styles, practitioners and texts. The course offers an exciting balance of creativity and critical thinking, preparing students for higher education and a wide range of careers.
Course Content
Create and perform original devised theatre.
Perform extracts from published plays for assessment.
Study influential theatre practitioners including Stanislavski, Brecht and Frantic Assembly.
Analyse and interpret contemporary and classical theatre texts.
Watch and evaluate live professional theatre productions.
Develop skills in acting, directing and design for performance.
Explore how theatre communicates meaning to an audience.
Entry Requirements
5 GCSEs at grade 4 or above, including Mathematics and English Language. It is not mandatory to have taken Drama GCSE.
How is it Assessed?
Component 1: Devising (40%)
Practical group performance and devising portfolio
Component 2: Text in Performance (20%)
Performance of a scripted extract and monologue
Component 3: Theatre Makers in Practice (40%)
Written examination and live theatre evaluation
Future Pathways with Drama
Acting, Directing, Theatre Production, Arts Administration, Media and Broadcasting, Film and Television, Teaching and Education, Event Management, Marketing and Communications, Law, Public Relations, Espionage, Creative Industries, Further Study in Drama, Theatre or Performing Arts

English Literature
English Literature A Level
Examining Board: Edexcel
Overview
One of the most respected and rewarding A Levels, English Literature is a gateway to exploring the human condition and engaging in critical debate about complex moral, social and cultural issues. This course is ideal for students who are curious about people, ideas and different perspectives.
Alongside studying a diverse selection of literary texts, you will have the opportunity to steer your own studies by choosing texts for independent study, pursuing themes and genres that interest you. There are also opportunities to visit a theatre, take part in a workshop with a visiting author and attend a Literature conference in London.
Course Content
Study A Streetcar Named Desire by Arthur Miller.
Investigate a range of novels before choosing your coursework focus.
Study Hamlet by Shakespeare.
Explore two powerful novels within the theme of ‘Women in Society’ – Wuthering Heights and A Thousand Splendid Suns.
Experience modern poetry and poetry from the Romantic period.
Entry Requirements
5 GCSEs at Grade 4 or above, including Mathematics and English Language, and Grade 5 in English, although Grade 6 is preferred.
How is it Assessed?
Paper 1: Drama (30%)
Paper 2: Prose (20%)
Paper 3: Poetry (30%)
NEA: Independent Study of two linked texts (20%)
Future Pathways with English Literature
Journalism, Creative Writing, Publishing, Politics and the Civil Service, Marketing and Public Relations, Media and Communications, Teaching and Education

French
French A Level
Examining Board: AQA
Overview
This course is about so much more than just developing your linguistic skills. Whilst you will undoubtedly flourish as a linguist and master an impressive range of vocabulary and grammar, A Level French also gives you an insight into contemporary issues in French-speaking societies.
The fascinating topics include examining social changes, music and the arts, architecture, politics and immigration, as well as the traditions and history of French-speaking countries – and we will discuss all of this in French! You will learn about the French dictatorship and the ever-changing political landscape of contemporary France and other French-speaking countries.
Course Content
La famille en voie de changement
La « cyber-société »
Le rôle du bénévolat
Les aspects positifs d'une société diverse
Quelle vie pour les marginalisés ?
Comment on traite les criminels
Une culture fière de son patrimoine
La musique francophone contemporaine
Cinéma : le septième art
Les ados, le droit de vote et l'engagement politique
Manifestations, grèves – à qui le pouvoir ?
La politique et l'immigration
Entry Requirements
5 GCSEs at Grade 4 or above, including Mathematics and English Language, and GCSE French Grade 6 – although in exceptional cases a Grade 5 may be considered.
How is it Assessed?
Paper 1 - Listening, reading and writing (50%)
Paper 2 – Writing (20%)
Paper 3 – Speaking exam, including IRP discussion (30%)
Future Pathways with French
Being a proficient French-speaker is a sought-after skill and A-Level French opens many doors. Many students go on to study French at university, often in combination with another subject such as International Relations, Politics and Business management and Economics. In terms of careers, French is useful for careers in business and finance, translation and interpreting, journalism, travel and tourism, diplomacy and civil service, and the education sector.

Art and Design
Art and Design A Level
Examining Board: AQA
Overview
This course encourages students to develop different approaches to recording images, such as observation, analysis, expression, and imagination. Students explore a wide range of techniques and materials while investigating artists, designers, and cultural influences using sketchbooks and journals to record their ideas.
Course Content
Drawing and painting from life
Exploring, using and creating with a wide range of materials
Developing ideas and themes from personal experience
2D and 3D techniques, including ceramics and sculptural forms
Mixed-media, including collage and assemblage
Entry Requirements
5 GCSEs at grade 4 or above, including Mathematics and English Language, and a Grade 5 or higher at GCSE Art, or an equivalent arts subject
How is it Assessed?
Component 1: Personal Investigation, including a 1000–3000-word essay explaining the development of your investigation (60%).
Component 2: Externally set assignment, concluding in a 15-hour exam to produce a final outcome for your studies. This runs between February and May in Year 13 (40%).
Future Pathways with Art and Design
Actor, Advertising, Animator, Architect, Art Therapist, Camera operator, Conservator, Content creator, Fashion Designer, Film Director, Game artist, Graphic Designer, Illustrator, Jeweller, Make-up Artist, Photographer, Prosthetic technician, Teacher, Web Designer, Interior stylist, Hair stylist or anything that needs a spark of creativity.
Art and design also develops your transferable skills such as creative problem-solving, independence, research, and communication that are valued by universities and employers.

Biology
Biology A Level
Examining Board: OCR A
Overview
Choosing A Level Biology gives you the opportunity to develop an exceptional range of skills all whilst learning about the living world around us from the cellular level all the way to whole ecosystems. A subject that combines deep learning, practical hands-on skills, problem solving, analytical thinking and clear communication, making you a true multi-disciplinarian
Topics include cell structure, biological molecules, gas exchange and circulatory systems, genetics, homeostasis, biodiversity all of which provide a broad foundation of knowledge to allow students to go on to study or work in the field of biology or support them in their applications to other STEM related fields such as sport sciences, engineering and nuclear medicine.
Course Content
Module 1: Development of Practical Skills in Biology
Module 2: Foundations in Biology
Module 3: Exchange and Transport
Module 4: Biodiversity, Evolution and Disease
Module 5: Communication, Homeostasis and Energy
Module 6: Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystem
Entry Requirements
5 GCSEs Grade 4 or above, including Grade 6 in Biology or 6-6 in Combined Science, Grade 6 in Maths, and Grade 4 in English Language.
How is it Assessed?
Paper 1: Biological Processes (37%)
Paper 2: Biological Diversity (37%)
Paper 3: Unified Biology (26%)
Practical Endorsement in Biology
Future Pathways with Biology
Being a proficient biologist opens many doors. Students go on to study a wide variety of biology related courses including Medicine, Veterinary Science, Dentistry, Biomedical Science, Biochemistry, Neuroscience, Pharmacology, Genetics, Biotechnology, Environmental Science, Ecology and Conservation, Physiotherapy and Forensic Science. The multidisciplinary nature of Biology makes it a fantastic subject to apply to a wide range of career choice including those outside of the STEM world including law, the civil service and the armed forces.

Chemistry
Chemistry A Level
Examining Board: OCR
Overview
Curious about how medicines are developed, how new materials are created, or how chemistry can help tackle climate change? OCR A Chemistry builds on your GCSE knowledge through practical experiments and real-world applications, developing the analytical, mathematical and problem-solving skills valued by universities and employers. You'll explore the science behind medicine, energy, sustainability and modern technology, gaining a deeper understanding of how chemistry shapes the world around us and opens doors to a wide range of STEM careers.
The course shows how chemistry is at the heart of modern science, industry and technology.
Course Content
Module 1 – Development of practical skills in chemistry: titrations, chemical analysis, organic synthesis
Module 2 – Foundations in chemistry: bonding, mole calculations, atomic structure
Module 3 – Periodic table and energy: group 2 and 7, energy in reactions
Module 4 – Core organic chemistry: alkanes, alkenes, alcohols and haloalkanes
Module 5 – Physical chemistry and transition elements: rate and equilibria, transition metals
Module 6 – Organic chemistry and analysis: carboxylic acids, benzene, nitrogen compounds, polymers and organic synthesis
Entry Requirements
5 GCSEs at grade 4 or above, including Mathematics and English Language, and grade 6 or above in Combined Science or Chemistry; Grade 6 or above in Mathematics.
How is it Assessed?
Paper 1: Periodic table, Elements and Physical Chemistry (37%)
Paper 2: Synthesis and Analytical Techniques (37%)
Paper 3: Unified Chemistry (26%)
Practical Endorsement in Chemistry
Future Pathways with Chemistry
Chemistry is highly valued by universities and employers, providing an excellent foundation for degrees in Medicine, Dentistry, Veterinary Science, Pharmacy, Chemistry and Engineering. The course develops practical, analytical and problem-solving skills that open doors to careers in healthcare, research, industry, environmental science, finance and many other STEM fields.

English Language
English Language A Level
Examining Board: AQA
Overview
In English Language everything is a text, from road signs to newspapers: political speeches to everyday conversations. You will learn how to break a text down for analysis and interpret how language is used to inform, entertain and shape representations of people, groups and ideas. You will also investigate how language varies according to factors such as region, gender, occupation, and social context.
This course is perfect for students who are curious about communication and the role language plays in shaping the world around us. Language lies at the heart of politics, trade, education, the media and our personal relationships. By studying English Language, you will gain a deeper understanding of how people use language to express identity, influence others and make meaning in everyday life.
Course Content
Language Change – cultural, technological and social
Language diversity – power, gender, region, occupation
Language in representation – diverse range of non-fiction texts
Child Language Development
Investigative Project
Entry Requirements
5 GCSEs at Grade 4 or above, including Mathematics and English Language, and Grade 5 in English, although Grade 6 is preferred.
How is it Assessed?
Paper 1: Language, the Individual and Society (40%)
Paper 2: Language Diversity and Change (Reading and Writing 40%)
NEA: Language in Action (20%)
Future Pathways with English Language
Journalism, Creative writing, Speech and Language Therapy, Business and Marketing, Education, Linguistics, Communications, further study at University.

Geography
Geography A Level
Examining Board: Edexcel
Overview
A Level Geography is a brilliant choice if you are curious about the world and want to understand the major issues shaping our future. You will explore fascinating topics such as climate change, natural hazards, globalisation, migration and changing places, helping you understand how people, places and environments are connected.
Geography also develops skills that universities and employers really value. Through fieldwork, research and data analysis, you will build confidence in problem-solving, decision-making and evaluating different viewpoints. It is a versatile subject that can lead to a huge range of university courses and careers, while giving you the knowledge to make sense of an ever-changing world.
Course Content
The carbon cycle and energy insecurity
The water cycle and water insecurity
Entry Requirements
5 GCSEs at Grade 4 or above, including Mathematics and English Language, and a Grade 5 at GCSE Geography (Grade 6 preferred).
How is it Assessed?
Paper 1: Physical Geography (30%)
Paper 2: Human Geography (30%)
Paper 3: Synoptic investigation (20%)
Future Pathways with Geography
A Level Geography is a highly versatile subject that can lead to a wide range of university courses, apprenticeships and careers. These include; Environmental Consultant, Urban and Town Planner, Climate Scientist, Sustainability Consultant, Geologist, Civil Engineer, Law, GIS and Mapping Specialist, International Development Worker, Disaster and Emergency Management, Conservation and Wildlife Management. Transport Planner, Geography Teacher, Renewable Energy and Environmental Management.

Business Studies
Business Studies A Level
Examining Board: AQA
Overview
The Business A Level course immerses students into real-world relevance, covering current issues like AI and globalisation as well as the core functions necessary to make a successful business. Learners will develop practical skills that are transferable, including data analysis and critical thinking, whilst using these skills in case-study scenarios - ensuring they apply their theory. An excellent way to delve into the world of work.
Course Content
Business and Objectives
Forms of Business and stakeholders
Marketing management
Financial management
Operations management
Managing business culture
Business and society
Business and the external environment
Strategy and planning
Change, risk and uncertainty
Entry Requirements
5 GCSEs at Grade 4 or above, including Maths and English Language. A Grade 5 in Maths is preferable.
How is it Assessed?
Paper 1: What is a Business? Managing Marketing and Finance (33%)
Paper 2: Managing People and Operations (33%)
Paper 3: Business and Society, the External Environment and Strategy (33%)
Future Pathways with Business
Entrepreneurship, Management Consulting, Marketing, Advertising, Financial Services, Corporate Finance, Product Development, Project Management, Human Resources, and much more.

Criminology
Criminology Applied Level 3 Diploma
Examining Board: WJEC
Overview
We are surrounded by stories, films and books about crime... but what is the reality? Criminology applies the scientific approach of Sociology and Psychology to ask questions about what we mean by crime, why people become criminal, how they are dealt with and whether our justice system is effective.
Course Content
How campaigns have led to changes in the law
Types of crime, why crimes may go unreported, and real-life-cases
Explanations of crime and how to reduce it
The role of police, courts, judges, and more
Ways to gather and assess evidence
Entry Requirements
5 GCSEs at grade 4 or above, including Mathematics and English Language.
How is it Assessed?
Year 12 – Certificate in Criminology. 50% Controlled Assessment and 50% Exam
Year 13 – Diploma in Criminology. 50% Controlled Assessment and 50% Exam
Future Pathways with Criminology
Criminology can lead to university courses in Criminology, Psychology, Sociology, Policing, Forensic Science, Social Work and Criminal Justice. It provides a strong foundation for careers in policing, probation, youth justice, prison services, forensic investigation, law, intelligence services, social work and community safety.

Economics
A Level Economics
Examining Board: AQA
Overview
Economics is a social science that studies human behaviour, especially why certain choices are made by individuals, businesses, and governments. We study how markets work and how they fail. In order to do so effectively, we study the dynamics of change at a micro level (i.e. individuals and companies), as well as at the macro levels of governments and international trading partners. You will develop the knowledge and skills needed to understand data, think critically about issues, and make decisions. Economics provides tools for improving how people can live better lives.
Course Content
Markets and the Price Mechanism
Individual Economic Decision Making
Monopolies and Oligopolies
Macroeconomic Indicators
Economic Growth and its Consequences
Inflation and Unemployment
Fiscal and Monetary Policy
International Economics and International Development
Distribution of Wealth and How Governments Manage the Economy
Entry Requirements
5 GCSEs at Grade 4 or above, including Mathematics and English Language, and a Science subject at Grade 4 or above.
How is it Assessed?
Paper 1: Markets and Market Failure (33%)
Paper 2: National and International Economics (33%)
Paper 3: Economics Principles and Issues (33%)
Future Pathways with Economics
Economics at A Level is highly regarded by both employers and universities due to the range and depth of study as well as the Assessment Objectives, which require significant intellectual rigour throughout the course.
A degree in the subject is the third highest paid occupation for new graduates and will open up opportunities in Finance, Business, Marketing, Government and Consultancy.
There are excellent Apprenticeship options, e.g. in the Government Economic Service, where we have seen our former students pursue very successful careers.
